theQuestionThisCardExistedToAnswer.question: Can Hays geometry be rebound to the parcel it belongs to without discarding the roughly 92,000 correct records?
theQuestionThisCardExistedToAnswer.answer: Yes, and the ceiling is 115,035 of 173,050 production rows. The county publishes the crosswalk in two columns the Orion parser dropped. 30,862 rows rebind to a different parcel, 19,902 gain geometry they do not have today, 64,271 are already right and stay exactly where they are, and 58,015 have no key and keep today's behaviour untouched. Nothing is withdrawn.

reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.instrument: hays_rebind_probe.py, written for this lane BEFORE reading CTX-HAYS-KEY's probe. File-based, --self-test (18 cases, four explicit non-vacuity assertions), --violate. main() REFUSES to score if the self-test fails.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.countingRule: roll = every data row of the Orion property export (134,592). matched = rows whose key resolves in the stated txgio index. situsAgree = matched rows where norm(CAD Situs) == norm(txgio situs_address), norm = uppercase then delete every non-[A-Z0-9]. Index keeps the LOWEST feature_index on a duplicated key, mirroring the bake's ORDER BY feature_index + keep-first. A blank key is not a key, and a BLANK-vs-BLANK situs comparison is NOT agreement.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.doTheyMatchCTX_HAYS_KEY: THE MATCHED COUNTS REPRODUCE EXACTLY. THE AGREEMENT COUNTS DO NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A FINDING.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.theWholeDifferenceIsBLANK_EQUALS_BLANK: re-running my scorer with the blank-counts-as-agreement rule reproduces CTX-HAYS-KEY's three numbers EXACTLY: 53, 108,759 (89.65) and 108,532 (94.35). The both-blank populations are 53, 1,316 and 1,295. The two instruments agree on every match and differ on ONE counting rule.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.whichRuleIsRight: the strict one, per ENFORCEMENT: absent, zero and unmeasured are three different states. Two rows that each carry no address are UNMEASURED against each other, not agreeing.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.andItMattersMOSTinTheDirectionThatDECIDE: today's key -- PropertyID to txgio prop_id -- agrees on situs on ZERO of 78,107 matched rows, not 53. Every one of CTX-HAYS-KEY's 53 was blank-vs-blank. The 0.07 percent figure the dispatch carried overstates today's key by its own entire margin; the honest figure is 0.00 percent. It strengthens the case, not weakens it.
reDerivedCrosswalkNumbers.andItCostsTheCANDIDATEKeysAboutAPointEac: PropertyNumber to geo_id is 93.22 percent, not 94.35. That residue is 1,295 both-blank pairs plus genuine formatting and vintage divergence between the 2026 CAD export and the 2025-03 StratMap drop. Reported, not smoothed.

CTX-HAYS-KEY's 38,444 prop_ids absent from the declared roll against my 38,533 prop_ids absent from the 2026-08-26 EXPORT: different denominators, 89 apart, recorded rather than rounded.

They reconcile by arithmetic: 173,050 nodes minus 38,533 non-account nodes = 134,517 account nodes, and 134,592 export accounts minus 134,517 = 75 accounts with no production node. Stated as arithmetic.

theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.name: the provenance record could claim a bind the geometry did not take
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.what: the first implementation derived provenance.parcelJoin.state and featureIndex from the OFFERED crosswalk row, while every geometry consumer read a separate `row` variable. Disabling the `row = crosswalkRow` assignment left the payload saying joined-crosswalk at feature 40337 while drawing feature 57725 -- a provenance record describing a bind that did not happen, which is worse than either outcome alone.
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.howFound: by violating the change, not by reading it, and specifically by noticing that the first probe made only ONE test fail. The shape of that single failure is what exposed it.
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.fix: the record derives from `crosswalkBound = crosswalkRow != null && row === crosswalkRow`, so it can only claim a bind the geometry actually took.
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.regressionControl: a test that reads the geometry side (the zoning stamp, which exists on only one of the two features) and the provenance side and asserts they agree. The same violation now fails 5 tests instead of 1.

theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.name: the parser's honest-null test was presence-shaped and on the wrong layer
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.what: it asserted only that HeaderIndex.get returns "" for a missing column. Replacing textOrNull(header.get(...)) with the raw header.get(...) in the PARSER left it PASSING while every row of such a county acquired an empty-string identifier -- a sentinel that satisfies a not-null check, identifies nothing, and would become a join key every row in the county shared.
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.howFound: violation run V5 passed when it should have failed. A violation that passes is the finding.
theTwoDefectsFoundBYVIOLATINGtheChange.fix: a real fixture (orion_no_identifier_columns_sample.csv, a property-classified header carrying neither column) run THROUGH the parser, asserting null on both. The same violation now fails.

twoDesignDecisionsThatCHANGEDunderMeasur.what: the migration originally carried a partial index on (county_fips, property_number). REMOVED.
twoDesignDecisionsThatCHANGEDunderMeasur.why: nothing queries cad_property by property_number -- the bake loads the county's declared-vintage rows by (county_fips, tax_year) and reads the column off rows it already has -- so the index is an artifact that exists, is correct, and does nothing. And this repo's schema fixture is a pg_dump of what drizzle-kit push builds from the DRIZZLE SCHEMA, not of what the migrations build: proven by 0095's txgio_parcel.geom AND txgio_parcel_geom_gist_idx, which are in that migration and live in production and appear NOWHERE in schema.sql.template. A migration-only index would have drifted the fixture and failed CI's own drift check.

twoDesignDecisionsThatCHANGEDunderMeasur.what: the geo_id fetch originally compared btrim(geo_id) = ANY(...). Now compares the raw column.
twoDesignDecisionsThatCHANGEDunderMeasur.why: measured: ZERO of Hays' 130,246 non-null geo_ids carry surrounding whitespace, so trimming changes no result and would permanently prevent a plain (county_fips, geo_id) index from being used. txgio_parcel has no geo_id index today and the situs join already pays that price -- it needed a 34-call functional index to escape it. The blank guard stays. A padded geo_id would produce a MISS, an honest geometry absence, never a wrong bind.
twoDesignDecisionsThatCHANGEDunderMeasur.cost: measured on staging: one 5,000-key chunk is 4.3 seconds without an index, so Hays' 115,035 keys are about 24 chunks and roughly 100 seconds of bake time. Named so the integration seat is not surprised.

lessonsForFleetMemory.text: A BLANK-VS-BLANK COMPARISON IS NOT AGREEMENT, AND IT MOVES HEADLINE NUMBERS BY ENOUGH TO CHANGE A DECISION. CTX-HAYS-KEY's three crosswalk agreement figures (53, 108,759, 108,532) reproduce EXACTLY under a counting rule that scores two empty situs strings as agreeing. Under a strict rule they are 0, 107,443 and 107,237. The one that matters: today's Hays key agrees on situs ZERO times out of 78,107, not 53. When re-deriving another lane's numbers, reproduce the MATCHED counts first -- if those agree exactly and the agreement counts do not, the difference is a counting rule, and one of the two is wrong.

A PROVENANCE FIELD DERIVED FROM A DIFFERENT VARIABLE THAN THE ONE THE CONSUMER READS WILL EVENTUALLY LIE. The crosswalk's parcelJoin.state was computed from the OFFERED row while geometry read a separate `row`. Disabling one line made the payload claim joined-crosswalk at feature 40337 while drawing 57725. Derive the record from the variable the consumers actually read (`row === crosswalkRow`), so the two cannot be edited apart.

A VIOLATION THAT MAKES ONLY ONE TEST FAIL IS ITSELF A FINDING. Disabling the crosswalk preference failed 1 test of 130. That was not reassurance that the change was small; it was the signal that the other assertions were reading provenance rather than geometry. After the fix the same violation fails 5.

TEST THE PARSER, NOT THE HELPER THE PARSER CALLS. An honest-null test that asserted HeaderIndex.get returns "" for a missing column PASSED while the parser was writing empty-string identifiers -- a sentinel that satisfies a not-null check and would become a join key every row in the county shared. Only a real fixture run through the parser caught it, and only because the violation probe was run.

THIS REPO'S SCHEMA FIXTURE MIRRORS `drizzle-kit push`, NOT THE MIGRATIONS. lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template is a pg_dump of what push builds from lib/db/src/schema. Proof: migration 0095's txgio_parcel.geom column and txgio_parcel_geom_gist_idx are in that migration and live in production and appear NOWHERE in the template. A migration-only index or column therefore FAILS CI's own drift check. Declare it in the drizzle schema, or do not add it.

DECLARE A NEW DRIZZLE COLUMN LAST. A fresh `drizzle-kit push` emits columns in declaration order; a migration's ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN appends. Declaring the new column last is what makes CI's fresh schema and the real production table have the SAME column order, so the fixture describes both.

MAKE A NEW RECORD FIELD REQUIRED AND LET THE TYPE CHECKER FIND THE PRODUCERS. Adding quickRefId/propertyNumber to CadPropertyRecord as REQUIRED surfaced two vendor parsers (dcad-certified, tad-propertydata) that grep for `propertyUseCode` had missed. A discriminated requirement the compiler enforces has no trigger to be missing and no call site to be absent.

NEVER MAP A GEOMETRY PUBLISHER'S KEY INTO THE APPRAISAL SIDE OF A CROSSWALK. The StratMap shapefile carries GEO_ID and the TAD export keys on gis_link; copying either into cad_property.property_number would make the crosswalk's two sides come from the same party and agree by construction. That is internal consistency wearing the shape of an agreement between derivations.

A TRIM ON THE COLUMN SIDE OF A JOIN PREDICATE PERMANENTLY DISABLES A PLAIN INDEX. `btrim(geo_id) = ANY(...)` cannot use a (county_fips, geo_id) btree. Measured: zero of Hays' 130,246 geo_ids carry padding, so the trim bought nothing and cost the index. The situs join already pays this and needed a 34-call functional index to escape it.

WHEN A DISPATCH NAMES A VIOLATION CASE, READ THE STORED RECORD BEFORE BUILDING TO IT. The dispatch said account 40138 must bind R26199's parcel and must fail to beforehand. Production shows it ALREADY binds it -- its claim is 2026-vintage so it was never contaminated. The parcel that actually fails is 26199, and it must move to R117015's parcel. Forward reasoning from the mechanism produced the dispatch's answer and it was wrong.
